messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Malayalam, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Malayalam line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
പക്ഷേ നീ എന്തുകൊണ്ട് ഇത്ര വലിയ അസ്വസ്ഥതയിലേക്ക് മടങ്ങുന്നു? നീ എന്തുകൊണ്ട് ആ ആനന്ദകരമായ മല കയറുന്നില്ല അത് എല്ലാ സന്തോഷത്തിന്റെ മൂലവും കാരണവുമാണ്?

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table (Malayalam translation)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Malayalam) | Back‑Translation (English) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------| | Ma | adversative conjunction “but” | പക്ഷേ | “but” | OK | | tu | 2nd person singular pronoun “you” | നീ | “you” | OK | | perché (1) | interrogative “why” (cause) | എന്തുകൊണ്ട് | “why” | OK | | ritorni | verb “return” (2 sg.) | മടങ്ങുന്നു | “returns” | OK | | a | preposition “to” (direction) | …യിലേക്ക് (as in *അസ്വസ്ഥതയിലേക്ക്*) | “to” | OK | | tanta | intensifier “so great” | ഇത്ര വലിയ | “so great” | OK | | noia | noun “annoyance / boredom” | അസ്വസ്ഥത | “discomfort / annoyance” | OK | | perché (2) | interrogative “why” (cause) | എന്തുകൊണ്ട് | “why” | OK | | non | negation particle “not” | — (negation fused in verb) | (negative) | **UNNECESSARY** (Malayalam expresses negation within the verb) | | sali | verb “ascend / climb” (2 sg.) | കയറുന്നു | “climbs” | OK | | il | definite article “the” | — (no article) | (none) | **UNNECESSARY** | | dilettoso | adjective “delightful / delectable” | ആനന്ദകരമായ | “delightful” | OK | | monte | noun “mountain” | മല | “mountain” | OK | | ch’è | relative pronoun + copula “which is” | അത് … ആണ് | “that … is” | OK | | principio | noun “source / principle, origin” | മൂലവും | “source / origin” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | — (conjoined by suffix *‑വും*) | (and) | **UNNECESSARY** | | cagion | noun “cause” | കാരണവും | “cause” | OK | | di | preposition “of” (genitive) | …യുടെ (as in *സന്തോഷത്തിന്റെ*) | “of” | OK | | tutta | universal quantifier “all / every” | എല്ലാ | “all / every” | OK | | gioia | noun “joy” | സന്തോഷം | “joy” | OK |
### Items flagged
- **UNNECESSARY**: `non`, `il`, `e` – Malayalam does not require separate negative particles, articles, or an explicit coordinating conjunction; the meaning is conveyed by verb morphology, lack of article, and the suffix *‑വും* respectively.
No source words are **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or suffer **GRAMMAR** mismatches in the translation.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Malayalam script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Malayalam text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
